reproducibilityNote: Before public release verification, Git's Windows CRLF-to-LF conversion was found to invalidate raw JSON hashes on Linux. This changes no measured flux or scientific decision; the initial implementation remains in Git history.

sources.title: The James Webb Space Telescope Absolute Flux Calibration. VI. Near-Infrared Camera Imaging and Coronagraphy
sources.resultPeriod: 3.5 years of standard observations; calibration incorporated March 2026
sources.claim: The official calibration includes a much broader standard set and full correction chain than this local audit. The present failure does not refute that calibration. Bibliographic title corrected in the catalogue.

sources.resultPeriod: Code used for Boyer 2026; remote HEAD independently checked on review date
details: do_aper_phot.py selects a nojump product only with jumpdq>0, EFFEXPTM<100 seconds and peakrate>5000 DN/s. find_star.py may produce a nojump product under a different condition: imaging, central bit4 and NGROUPS>2. Generation and later selection must not be conflated.

find_star.py prepares data_cut near the source but assigns peakrate=np.nanmax(data), the full image. A low local cutout peak does not prove that this global threshold fails. No claim is made that the official branch was executed here.

do_aper_phot.py uses default exact aperture overlap, standard-deviation sigma clipping, and interpolation for eligible NaN cases. RC73 instead used midpoint overlap, MAD clipping and finite-value sums. The present audit isolates overlap and one sky variant; it is not execution of the full official pipeline.

do_aper_correction.py evaluates PSF aperture fractions with the same aperture and background annulus. make_psfmodels.py and the README describe per-image OPD, source spectrum and position. Multi-radius PSF prediction is established methodology, not a newly invented calibration technique.

sources.claim: Exact circle-pixel overlap and subpixel sampling are distinct geometrical operators. Exact here describes integration of pixel values, not reconstruction of unmeasured intra-pixel optical structure.
Jump detection works on ramps and can be affected by preceding corrections. Absence of a CAL central flag is not a complete test of all ramp-processing effects.

sources.resultPeriod: Initial submission 2019-04-12; accessed version v3 revised 2020-07-06
sources.claim: Weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift relies on the appropriate distributional structure and density ratio. It is not a remedy for unconstrained unobserved intensities or arbitrary conditional measurement changes. No new coverage theorem is claimed.

sources.resultPeriod: March 2026 imaging calibration, distinct from September review date
sources.claim: Official calibration and standard programmes provide source context; local remeasurement is reported as repository analysis, not as a new STScI result.

confirmedComputations: Independent circle quadrature and antiderivative implementations agree within 1.34e-15 relative flux on complete apertures, compared with the 1e-8 numerical criterion.
Accurate integration leaves WDFS0458-56 F090W maximum excursion 0.023007474691628893 and NRCB1 cross-star F090W pattern difference 0.02149348931191042.

The finite 9-center x 2-background family gives an optimistic pattern-2 deficit lower bound 0.02224362272009206. The inequality uses the deficient flux upper bound and other flux lower bounds; all eighteen choices per exposure are enclosed.

Two NRCA3 exposures have one non-finite r5 pixel each, with missing weights 0.6029151829952866 and 0.5204661838335453 square pixels. Full flux is null; both groups retain all four identities but only three complete apertures.

The deficient WDFS0458-56 F090W pattern2 has no bit4 pixel within r2. Pattern3 has three, while WDFS0122-30 F090W pattern4 has one. This defeats a simple co-location claim, not every possible jump effect.
changedStates: UP-003 remains open: a finite numerical rescue family is rejected; NRCA3 complete-aperture support corrected.
UP-625 remains open: missing-area completeness is separated from flux identifiability; no coverage guarantee added.
inferences: The tested numerical and small-center/background choices are insufficient to explain the local failure.
Missing pixels in NRCA3 do not explain the separate complete NRCB1 deficit.
A measured missing-area fraction is not a flux-error bound without a constraint on unobserved intensity.
unverifiedProposals: Use four per-image physical PSFs to predict concentration ratios and corrected multi-radius flux without fitting to total flux.
Validate missing-pixel reconstruction by star-separated masking on complete development images, then use a separately locked fresh-star test.
causalModel: Converted pixels and complete support -> measurable numerical nuisance family -> residual survives every member -> independent multi-radius PSF predictions -> fresh-star calibration -> separate spatial/crowding bridge -> distance-ladder assessment. No downstream implication is asserted in this cycle.

failuresPreserved: RC73 numerical outcomes and records were not overwritten.
First RC74 strict integration failed at a non-finite aperture pixel. The revised diagnostic retains all exposure identities and null full flux, without qualification or imputation.
Exact integration did not rescue the failed NRCB1 F090W gates.
The optimistic finite-family bound remains above 2%; no setting was selected as a successful correction.
Independent arithmetic agreement in RC73 did not establish independent pixel geometry. RC74 extends the audit to geometry but still shares extraction, units, centers and sky inputs.

uncertainty.numerical: Observed maximum change 0.010073%; independently checked geometry and sums.
uncertainty.background: Observed two-estimator sensitivity 0.003328%; not a bound on structured sky.
uncertainty.centering: Observed finite-grid sensitivity 0.142660%; offsets are not a confidence region and do not bound every continuous center.
uncertainty.measurement: ERR and correlated noise were not measured in this cycle. No significance or total uncertainty is reported.
uncertainty.model: OPD, spectrum, intra-pixel response, ramp effects and reconstruction model remain unquantified.
uncertainty.sampling: Four repeated exposures and few stars do not establish population coverage.
uncertainty.extrapolation: No full-detector, crowded-field, distance or H0 transfer claim.
